## Preparatory material

This book chapter on [“Crime Mapping: Spatial and Temporal Challenges”](https://www.librarysearch.manchester.ac.uk/permalink/44MAN_INST/1rfd42k/cdi_springer_books_10_1007_978_0_387_77650_7_2) from 2009 by Jerry Ratcliffe in the Handbook of Quantitative Criminology provides a brief but useful introduction to the relevance of crime mapping for criminology research and criminal justice practice.

* Those taking the course as a postgraduate course unit ought to watch also this [16 minute lecture (Links to YouTube)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dheAqmXvoBY) by Luc Anselin on “Geospatial Visualisation and ESDA”.

## Browser check

- Laptop or tablet. Recent Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.
- Press **Run Code**. Wait ~1 min the first time.
- You should see a map.


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
ward_url <- paste0("https://services1.arcgis.com/ESMARspQHYMw9BZ9/arcgis/rest/services/",
                   "Wards_December_2024_Boundaries_UK_BGC/FeatureServer/0/query?where=",
                   URLencode("LAD24NM='Leeds'", reserved = TRUE), "&outFields=WD24NM&outSR=4326&f=geojson")
download.file(ward_url, "leeds_wards.geojson", quiet = TRUE)
leeds_wards <- st_read("leeds_wards.geojson", quiet = TRUE)
ggplot(leeds_wards) + geom_sf() + labs(title = "The 33 wards of Leeds") + theme_void()
```
:::


No map? Try another browser, or let me know before the session.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Optional: use RStudio instead
- Install [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) and [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).
- Run once: `install.packages(c("sf", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "jsonlite", "classInt", "ggspatial", "RColorBrewer", "spatstat", "spdep"))`
- All workshop code runs unchanged. The data loads from the web.
:::
